newsitem.title: JAMAICA: CRICKET-LARA, HOOPER PUT WEST INDIES IN CONTROL.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-LARA, HOOPER PUT WEST INDIES IN CONTROL.

text.p: Inspired batting by Carl Hooper and Brian Lara put the West Indies in control on the first day of the first test match against India at Sabina Park on Thursday.

After India's bowlers had the better of the opening stages, Hooper and Lara took the game by the scruff of the neck as the home team, having won the toss and chosen to bat, reached 300 for four wickets by the close.
By the end of play, Hooper was was unbeaten on 87, having hit 13 glorious fours in his 131-ball, 162-minute innings, while night watchman Ian Bishop was on three.
Lara made 83 before, to the huge relief of the tourists, he fell to the second new ball for 83, his innings including 10 fours off the 141 balls he faced.
Earlier, Shivnarine Chanderpaul hit a half century while opener Sherwin Campbell made 40.
For India, debutant paceman Abey Kuruvilla took two wickets including Lara's, finishing the day with two for 46 from 18 overs.

The West Indies were 143 for three when Hooper, batting at number five, joined Lara at the crease. The pair added 147 runs in 142 minutes before Lara fell, brilliantly caught down the legside by wicket-keeper Nayan Mongia off Kuruvilla.
The Indians had controlled the first half of the day and broke through when Kuruvilla bowled the recalled Stuart Williams for 23 with the score at 41.

Campbell and the left-handed Chanderpaul played watchfully to add 55 for the second wicket but just when they seemed to be freeing themselves, Campbell edged the ball to Mongia off spinner Sunil Joshi.

Chanderpaul, apparently inspired by the arrival of Lara, accelerated to his twelfth test half century but after adding two more runs, he drove loosely at seamer Venkatesh Prasad and edged an easy catch to Mongia.
Lara and the incoming Cooper then thrilled the modest crowd, their 100 partnership coming up in 105 minutes off 173 balls.
